title: ThermalScope + Elasticity Dial for Dedicated GPU Pools
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Design an operational surface for Dedicated GPU pools focused on quickly assessing fleet health and tuning autoscaling/bursting in a single compact panel. This ticket delivers two primary UI patterns: (1) ThermalScope — a small-multiples thermal map that surfaces per-node temperature bands, memory pressure, and inferred throttling risk; and (2) Elasticity Dial — a contextual control (slider + quick-presets) for tuning autoscale sensitivity and short-term burst allowance. Goal: give SREs and platform engineers a low-cognitive way to diagnose emergent thermal/memory issues and apply controlled capacity adjustments without leaving the pool view.
updates: 2026-02-28: Kickoff with PM and Eng. Agreed success metrics: reduce incident triage time by 25% for capacity-related incidents and reduce unnecessary scale-ups during thermal events.

2026-03-03: Concept sketches and wireframes reviewed — two variants: grid-based ThermalScope vs. stacked sparkline lanes. Decided to prototype grid ThermalScope first based on rapid visual scanability.
2026-03-06: Low-fi prototype linked to Figma. Front-end feasibility sync: React + D3 minimal bundle; Eng requested simplified animation to avoid CPU spikes on large clusters.
2026-03-09: PM requested inclusion of cost delta preview in Elasticity Dial (estimated cost per hour for selected sensitivity). Added a cost preview chip to the dial.
2026-03-12: Accessibility pass started (colorblind-safe palette, keyboard focus on dial, aria live regions for thermal alerts).
2026-03-14: Hi-fi prototype and interaction spec completed. Hand-off to FE with acceptance criteria, tokenized color map, and microcopy.
acceptance_criteria: ThermalScope shows per-node temperature band (cool/warm/hot) and memory pressure for a 50-node pool in 2s or less in staging with synthetic data.
Elasticity Dial allows three presets (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) and a custom slider; applying a change emits an audit event and shows estimated hourly cost delta.
All interactive elements meet WCAG AA contrast and keyboard operability; automated a11y checks added to CI.
Design handoff includes CSS tokens, focus states, micro-interaction GIFs, and a list of required telemetry fields (node_temperature_celsius, gpu_util, gpu_memory_used_percent, throttling_events_1m).
Documentation: Console release notes and short runbook card describing when to use each Elasticity Dial preset.
review_feedback: Design review 2026-03-10: Eng asked to avoid per-node heatmap detail by default; we added a roll-up row and 'expand node' affordance.
SRE review 2026-03-11: Request to flag nodes with >3 throttling_events in the last minute — added alert badge state and tooltip with recent samples.
PM review 2026-03-12: Confirmed business rule: Elasticity Dial 'Aggressive' must still respect customer quota and Dedicated pool max cap; we added guard rails in spec.
notes: Telemetry: requires new aggregated metrics endpoint for 1m and 5m rollups to avoid expensive per-node queries in the console. ENG to add caching layer.
Performance: animations limited to 60fps and disabled when node-count > 200 to preserve client CPU. Consider server-side rendered SVG snapshots for very large pools.
Data retention: use recent 15m window for thermal triggers; correlate with kernel driver throttling metrics where available.
Fallback: if telemetry fields missing, ThermalScope shows 'data unavailable' state and Elasticity Dial disables presets that require cost estimates.
